summary_paragraph: A 46-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and obesity was admitted for acute-on-chronic abdominal pain and inability to tolerate oral intake, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She was treated with IV fluids, insulin for hyperglycemia, and medications for nausea and pain. A central line was placed due to difficult IV access. Imaging showed no obstruction or perforation. Her renal function improved with hydration, and she gradually advanced to a regular diet. She was discharged home in stable condition with referrals to GI and OB/GYN for ongoing management of gastroparesis and postmenopausal bleeding, respectively.
